title: Retry Strategy Simulator and Inspection Hub
creator: Rohan Patel
description: Design a lightweight interactive simulator and inspection hub in the Redwood Console that lets engineers and on-call owners: (1) visually simulate retry policies across historical failed request traces, (2) step through payload diffs and KV-cache state snapshots, (3) map observed error variants to an extensible taxonomy with recommended mitigations, and (4) preview the effect of configuration changes (retry backoff, max attempts, fallback model) on success rate and cost. The primary goal is to reduce MTTI/MTTR by giving operators a safe, replay-capable UI that surfaces hypotheses and the expected tradeoffs of retry/rollout choices without requiring full cluster replays or manual experiment runs.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive timeline view can replay a failed request and show where retries would have been attempted (visual markers) for at least three common retry policies: exponential backoff, fixed, and immediate
Payload diff inspector shows original and post-retry payloads side-by-side with field-level highlights and the ability to fold/unfold JSON nodes
Error taxonomy pane surfaces top-5 variants for a selected trace with one-click mitigation suggestions (e.g., increase timeout, switch model variant, add deduplication) and links to runbooks
Simulator computes an estimated cost delta and success probability for a given retry policy and displays a per-request token estimate and aggregated projection for the selected trace set
Prototype has Figma flows and a clickable HTML prototype linked in the ticket and receives design + eng sign-off in review meeting
decisions: Keep simulator read-only vs. live-toggle: MVP will be read-only and operate on sampled historical traces to avoid data drift and risk
Avoid server-side replays in MVP: compute estimates client-side from aggregated telemetry and known cost-per-token models
Expose only three policy knobs in the primary UI (max attempts, backoff multiplier, base delay) to reduce cognitive load
tradeoffs: Accuracy vs. speed: client-side estimations sacrifice precise end-to-end fidelity but enable fast iteration and safe preview
Privacy vs. utility: showing payload fields helps debugging but requires scrubbing or opt-in access controls for PII-sensitive customers
Scope vs. complexity: not implementing model-in-the-loop simulation (i.e., running a model on replayed payloads) keeps MVP feasible but may understate some failure modes
